title: How 54% of points wins 80% of tennis matches
description:
Roger Federer won almost 80% of his 1,526 singles matches but only 54% of the points. Tennis scoring stacks races: win 54% of points at random and you take 60% of games (first to 4, win by 2), 76% of sets (first to 6, win by 2) and 86% of best-of-three matches. A lucky streak can steal a point or a game, but rarely a whole set, so a small edge grows at every level.

Numbers checked in code (exact game/set/match chances plus 100,000 simulated matches, every point 54% independent). Source: Federer's 2024 Dartmouth commencement address, home.dartmouth.edu/news/2024/06/2024-commencement-address-roger-federer

beats.say: He won 54% of points, and 80% of matches.
Roger Federer didn't save it for the big points. Give every point the same 54% chance, and the scoring does the rest.
Step one: points into games. You need 4 points, and you have to win by 2. Your 54 becomes 60%.
Step two: games into sets. First to 6 games, win by 2. Now you take 76% of sets.
But each step just counts wins of the one below. So where's the extra edge coming from?
A lucky streak can steal a point, even a game. To steal a set, it has to keep going, and it rarely does.
Step three: best of 3 sets. 86% of matches.
54% of points, 86% of matches. Real opponents vary, so Federer's number was 80. Barely half the points was enough.
So if you win 51% of points, what share of matches is that?
